user.title: Create presence sensor
user.description: This creates one presence sensor from motion plus one or more control entities. A control can be a door, a TV switch, a helper, or anything else that says presence should be held.

data.name: Presence sensor name
data.fresh_window: Control change grace time in seconds
data.control_closed_mode: How many controls must be closed/active?
data.unavailable_behavior: What should happen if a selected source is unavailable?

data_description.name: The name Home Assistant will show for the new presence sensor.
data_description.door_entities: Pick every binary sensor, switch, input boolean, fan, light, remote, or media player that should control presence holding. Examples: a closed door, a TV that is playing, an appliance that is running, a helper, or a fan.
data_description.motion_entities: Pick every motion sensor that can see movement in this room or area.
data_description.default_cooldown: Seconds. This is the starting value for each motion sensor. You can adjust each one later. The timer starts when the selected controls become closed/active.
data_description.fresh_window: Seconds. After the controls open or become closed/active, keep the presence sensor on no matter what. Use 15 if you are not sure.
data_description.control_closed_mode: Choose All when every selected control must be closed/active before presence can be held. Choose Any when one closed/active control is enough, like a TV being on.
data_description.unavailable_behavior: Choose whether a missing, unknown, or unavailable selected source should make this presence sensor unavailable, or should simply count as inactive/off.
data_description.show_debug_attributes: Off by default. Turn this on only while troubleshooting to show detailed source states, evaluations, timers, cooldowns, and pending confirmations.
data_description.no_motion_timeout_minutes: Minutes. When presence is being held while controls are closed/active, turn it off after this many minutes with no motion. Use 60 for one hour. Use 0 to disable this limit.
data_description.open_no_motion_timeout_minutes: Minutes. When the controls are open/off, keep presence on this long after all motion sensors turn off. Use 0 to follow motion immediately.

control_state.title: Teach one control
control_state.description:
Control {control_number} of {control_total}: **{control_name}** (`{control_entity_id}`).

Put the real thing in a state that should hold presence. Close the door, play or pause the TV, start the appliance, or turn the helper on. Home Assistant says this entity is currently `{current_state}`.

Choose every state that should hold presence.

data_description.control_active_state: Select one or more states. For example, a media player can hold presence while Playing or Paused.

motion_cooldown.title: Teach one motion sensor
motion_cooldown.description:
Motion sensor {motion_number} of {motion_total}: **{motion_name}** (`{motion_entity_id}`).

Enter how long this sensor must still say `on` after the controls become closed/active before presence is confirmed. Right now it says `{current_state}`.

Example: if you want it to still be on 3 minutes after closing the door, enter `180`.

data_description.motion_cooldown: How many seconds this motion sensor must still be on after the controls become closed/active.

error.no_motions: Select at least one motion sensor.
error.same_source_roles: Do not select the same entity as both a control and a motion sensor.
error.self_reference: The generated presence sensor cannot use itself as a source.
error.presence_cycle: A presence sensor cannot depend on itself through another Advanced Presence Detection helper.
error.no_active_states: Select at least one closed/active state.
